inputs.source: Published HR policy index content, authored by HR content team, two-person reviewed, read-only to the agent

instructions.note: 'Do not give legal advice' is enforced only by model compliance. No technical control (classifier, filter) checks or blocks legal-advice-like output.

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to policy index
controls.decay_rationale: The agent's credential cannot read or act beyond the policy index regardless of model behavior. It would need to be widened if the index's data scope expands, per control_decay.md (data_scope_expansion).

controls.name: Two-person review required before publishing HR policy content
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by human process before content enters the index the agent reads; does not depend on the agent's model capability.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the chat client outside the model; removes a common covert-channel exfiltration vector regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Network-layer egress denial, verified by penetration test
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer, independent of agent or model behavior, and verified by pen testing. It would be defeated only if the network policy itself is changed (control_removal), not by ordinary model or prompt behavior.

controls.name: Model pinned; version change requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: A model upgrade can only occur through a reviewed change ticket, not silently. This delays rather than prevents the model_upgrade trigger.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: do not give legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Relies entirely on the model continuing to follow the instruction. A more capable or adversarially prompted model could rationalize exceptions (ASI01).

findings.title: Internal policy content (reviewed, HR-authored) flows through search into the chat reply, with autonomy bounds undeclared

attack_path.note: Internal, two-person-reviewed policy content enters the agent's context via retrieval.
Agent reads the published policy index with a read-only, least-privilege credential.
Agent quotes retrieved policy content back to the authenticated requester's chat session.

forecast.watch_signal: The policy index begins including non-published, confidential, or restricted content (for example compensation or legal detail) without a corresponding re-scoping of the agent's read credential and a fresh risk assessment.

evidence.observation: Policy index holds only published policies, internal sensitivity, write restricted to HR content team, two-person review required to publish.
Agent credential is read only and scoped to the policy index (least privilege).
Replies go only to the authenticated requester's chat session; client does not render images or auto-fetch links.
No other tools, no memory, no network egress; egress denial verified by pen test.
Model is pinned; a model change requires a change ticket.
Autonomy is A3; no human approval gate on any capability.
'Use policy_search to find the relevant policy and quote it' directs the data flow from in.policy_docs through cap.policy_search to cap.chat_reply.
'Do not give legal advice' is a behavioral, model-dependent constraint on the chat reply.
max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not specified anywhere in the artifacts; per rubric section 4 this is treated as null/null, which triggers the autonomy modifier for an S2 sink.

recommendations.action: Declare and enforce explicit max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes for the agent so the design does not default to an unbounded-autonomy reading.

Gate any future expansion of the policy index to confidential or restricted content behind re-scoping of the agent's read credential and a fresh risk assessment, per ISO 42001 8.2 significant-change triggers.
Log chat replies with cited policy sources for audit and repudiation resistance.
Supplement the 'no legal advice' instruction with an output check, since the instruction alone is model-dependent and will decay under model_upgrade.

rating.rationale: Single finding drives the rating. Inherent is high: an internal (two-person reviewed) source reaching an internal-data egress sink (chat reply) is moderate under the base matrix, bumped one tier because the artifacts declare no explicit max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes for an S2 sink. Residual drops to low: four independent structural controls (scoped read-only credential, two-person publish review, non-rendering chat client, pen-test-verified network egress denial) earn the step-3 credit, and the behavioral 'no legal advice' instruction earns the step-4 credit. None of the controls sever the path outright, since reading and relaying policy content is the agent's intended function. Forecast rises to moderate under data_scope_expansion: if the policy index were ever widened to confidential or restricted content, the scoped-credential control would need to widen with it per control_decay.md, and the sink would become S3; the remaining structural and behavioral controls hold the projected risk at moderate rather than critical.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP config, IaC, or network policy export was provided; the egress denial and its pen-test verification are taken as declared in the runtime notes, not independently re-verified by this assessment.

max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes were not specified in any artifact; they are treated as null per the rubric, which triggers the autonomy risk modifier. Explicit bounds, if they exist, could lower the inherent rating.
No source code for policy_search.search was reviewed; the injection-safety of its 'query' parameter is inferred only from the tool schema.
